properties.decision:
PROPOSED, APPROVER `who:ajs`. His shape, 2026-08-10: *"maybe we do a top 4 and bottom 1 that always appears in the where-am-i?"*

TWO CONSTRAINTS HE STATED IN THE SAME BREATH, AND BOTH LOWER THE BAR ON PURPOSE.

(1) APPROXIMATION IS EXPLICITLY ACCEPTABLE: *"this doesn't have to be an exact 'what is the most pressing decision'. getting something in the general ballpark of what decisions I need to make or a rough 'top 5' is better than an equal set of 60+ decisions."* THIS IS AN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION AND IT SHOULD BE READ AS ONE. It means the ranking need not be defensible item by item — only roughly right at the head — which disposes of the standing objection that every candidate signal is too noisy. A flat list of 83 is the baseline being beaten, and it is a low bar. RECORDED BECAUSE THE OPPOSITE INSTINCT IS THE DEFAULT ONE: this project's habit is to refuse to compute what it cannot compute honestly, and here the user has said in advance that rough is what he wants.

(2) UNRANKED IS NOT DISCARDED: *"it is not like we are throwing the unmade decisions aside and saying 'these are not ranked well, therefore not important and we'll never make a decision on them'."* Nothing leaves the pile by ranking low, and the display must not read as a shortlist of what matters.

⭐⭐ AND HE NAMED THE FLAW HIMSELF, WHICH IS WHY THE SHAPE HAS FIVE SLOTS AND NOT FOUR: *"which has a side effect of saying things not searched for are not important, which is not true."*

⇒ THE BOTTOM SLOT IS THE EXPLORATION TERM, ARRIVED AT INDEPENDENTLY AND FROM THE OTHER DIRECTION. `dec:attention-is-measured-behaviourally-not-lexically` records, from the reinforcement-learning framing, that any attention ranking reinforces what has already been visited — so a node nothing surfaces is never read, never accumulates, and never rises, permanently; and that the standard remedies are an exploration term or optimistic initialisation. Anthony reached the same requirement from the user-experience side, before seeing that consequence applied. **THE TOP FOUR ARE EXPLOITATION AND THE BOTTOM ONE IS EXPLORATION.** A convergence from two independent directions is the strongest evidence this design gets that a property is real rather than clever.

THE SUBTLETY THAT DECIDES WHETHER THE BOTTOM SLOT WORKS AT ALL: "bottom 1" IS NOT A RANK, IT IS A HUGE TIE. Under any attention signal, everything never surfaced scores identically — measured 2026-08-10, 61 of 83 open decisions govern nothing and would sit in that tie under a consequence ranking too. So the slot needs a TIEBREAK, and the choice of tiebreak is the whole design:
  - DETERMINISTIC (always the same one) STARVES THE REST and is the failure mode dressed as a feature.
  - RANDOM among the never-touched is ε-greedy proper, and samples the set over time.
  - OLDEST-UNSEEN is random's better-behaved cousin: it guarantees coverage instead of merely expecting it, and it makes the slot's promise checkable.

COVERAGE IS COMPUTABLE AND SHOULD BE STATED RATHER THAN FELT: one slot per orientation against 61 unranked items is 61 orientations to see them all once. That is months at any normal cadence. If that is too slow the answer is more slots or an oldest-first draw, and the number is the argument — not a preference.

WHAT THIS SHAPE DOES NOT DEPEND ON, and why it can ship first: the slot structure is independent of HOW the top four are ranked. Any signal fills it — consequence (`dec:idea-a-critical-path-through-the-undecided`), attention (`dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`), or the already-accepted rule in `req:what-next` that an unmade decision outranks the work waiting on it. IT IS THEREFORE BUILDABLE BEFORE EITHER OPEN QUESTION IS SETTLED, using whatever ranking exists, which makes it the smallest useful increment in this whole thread.

TWO THINGS THE DISPLAY MUST SAY, given constraint (2): that the bottom slot is a DELIBERATE sample of the unranked and not the least important thing, and how many open decisions are not shown. A five-item list that silently stands for 83 is the false completeness `where-am-i` already forbids ("never report from a page as if it were the whole set").

OPEN, NOT SETTLED HERE: the tiebreak (random vs oldest-unseen); whether four is the right exploitation width; whether the ranking behind the top four is one merged score or two lists; and whether the same shape belongs in `loop_status` as well as `where-am-i`.
properties.name: PROPOSED — where-am-i shows four ranked open decisions and one deliberately UNRANKED, and a rough ranking is explicitly good enough
properties.rationale:
Anthony's shape, recorded as its own Decision rather than folded into either open ranking question because it is separable from both and shippable before either — the slot structure works with any ranking, including the one `req:what-next` already accepts. Folding it into a brainstorm node would bury the one piece of this thread that can be built now.

The convergence is the part worth preserving. The exploration requirement was derived an hour earlier from the Q-table framing as a consequence nobody had asked for; Anthony proposed the bottom slot from the user-experience side without reference to it. Two independent derivations of the same property is stronger evidence than either, and a later session that finds only one of them would be free to drop it as over-engineering.

The acceptance criterion is recorded as prominently as the shape because it cuts against this project's own reflex. reflow2 repeatedly refuses to compute what it cannot compute honestly — `dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement` is the canonical case. Here the user has pre-authorised a rough answer, and without that on the record the natural instinct is to refuse to rank at all and ship nothing.
